articles.title: Starship Reaches Orbit for the First Time on Flight 14, Deploys 26 Next-Gen Starlink Satellites
articles.summary: Starship's 14th test flight reached orbit for the first time on Monday, despite one engine shutting down unexpectedly mid-flight, deploying 26 next-generation Starlink V3 satellites one by one from a Pez-dispenser-style mechanism at roughly 269km altitude before the mission ended early. Each Starship can now carry about 60 Starlink V3 satellites, roughly 20 times the capacity of a Falcon 9 launch, and the new satellites offer around 10x the downlink and 22x the uplink capacity of the previous V2 generation, capability SpaceX needs to support Musk's stated goal of Starlink eventually carrying a majority of the world's internet traffic.

articles.title: Nvidia Puts Agent Monitoring Directly on the BlueField-4 DPU, Off the Host an Agent Could Compromise
articles.summary: Nvidia's Open Agent Safety Platform pairs OpenShell, a sandboxed runtime running on its Vera CPU, with Sentry, a monitoring layer that runs in silicon on the BlueField-4 DPU rather than on the same host as the agent it's watching. The architectural bet is physical separation as a security property: in a Vera Rubin POD, each compute tray's BlueField-4 sits on the node's only path to the model, meaning every agent "thought" has to pass through that chip, giving it both the best observation point and a hardware kill switch, isolated from the host and beyond the agent's own reach even if the host itself gets compromised.

articles.title: VSMC Opens First 300mm Fab in Singapore, VIS-NXP Joint Venture Hits 99%+ Yields
articles.summary: VisionPower Semiconductor Manufacturing Company, a joint venture between Vanguard International Semiconductor and NXP, opened its first 300mm wafer fab in Tampines, Singapore, completed in just 22 months and now in risk production after its first sample lot cleared yields above 99%. The fab targets mature nodes between 130nm and 40nm for power management, mixed-signal, analog, and interposer chips serving automotive, industrial, consumer, mobile, and HPC customers, with volume manufacturing starting Q1 2027 and full capacity, roughly 44,000 wafers a month and 1,600 jobs, targeted by 2029.

articles.title: Tesla's Optimus Hands Still Aren't Reliable Enough for Mass Production, Report Says
articles.summary: Tesla ramped Optimus production from a few dozen units in Q2 to several hundred a week last month, but the company is hitting real engineering roadblocks on the path to its 20,000-units-a-week target for year-end. Most units built so far aren't shipping to customers at all, instead staying in-house for testing and data collection, and are still confined to simple, repetitive tasks rather than functioning as general-purpose machines. The core problem is durability and reliable assembly of the hands, a struggle Tesla has reportedly wrestled with for over a year, and rather than relying on touch sensors built directly into the hand itself, the company is now developing a hot-swappable "sensing glove" as a workaround.

articles.title: New ROS 2 Node Definition Language Framework
articles.summary: Announced at ROSCon Global 2026 in Toronto, the NODL framework provides a metadata language to formally describe the ROS interface of a robotic node, including its topics, parameters, services, and actions. It allows developer tools to validate configuration layouts, auto-generate boilerplate code, and create automated testing setups directly from declarative node specifications. For anyone designing embedded control software or complex sensor integrations, this tool offers a standardized way to ensure subsystem nodes communicate reliably without manual, error-prone integration checks.

articles.title: AMD Acquires World Labs
articles.summary: AMD has agreed to acquire World Labs, a startup specializing in spatial intelligence and deep learning models designed to understand the physical three-dimensional world. This merger aims to build an open, end-to-end AI ecosystem by combining frontier physical intelligence research directly with high-performance silicon development. This acquisition is exceptionally relevant to those building physical machines because it bridges the gap between hardware acceleration and the spatial awareness foundation models required for next-generation robotic manipulation and navigation.

articles.title: VAST Data's DataEnclave Uses Nvidia Confidential Computing to Run AI Models Directly Inside Locked-Down Data
articles.summary: VAST Data unveiled DataEnclave, a confidential AI runtime built on NVIDIA Confidential Computing, aimed at industries like finance, healthcare, and government where sensitive data can't leave tightly controlled environments and outside AI models normally can't reach it. The system creates hardware-isolated secure enclaves using CPU and GPU trusted execution environments, requiring cryptographic attestation that verifies the environment and its enforced policy before any decryption key is released, so proprietary model weights and sensitive customer data get decrypted only inside a verified enclave and stay encrypted in both CPU and GPU memory while processing, invisible even to the infrastructure operator running the hardware.

articles.title: TSMC's 2024 $1T-by-2030 Forecast Was Already $700B Too Low
articles.summary: At TSMC's OIP North America symposium, VP Sajiv Dalal now projects the semiconductor industry hitting roughly $1.7 trillion by year-end, with AI alone crossing $1 trillion, dwarfing TSMC's own "aggressive" 2024 forecast of $1 trillion for the whole industry by 2030. TSMC's revenue is up 53.3% year-over-year through August, and new tape-outs have quadrupled across the N5, N3, and N2 nodes, with N2 seeing an especially sharp acceleration in new chip designs.

articles.title: Mastering the ROS RMW Workshop
articles.summary: This repository contains the training materials, benchmarks, and hands-on exercises for a technical workshop focused on tuning ROS 2 middleware performance.

articles.title: Samsung Electro-Mechanics Invests 6.78 Trillion Won in AI Chip Package Substrates
articles.summary: Samsung Electro-Mechanics is investing a combined 6.78 trillion won ($4.9 billion) to expand FC-BGA substrate production, 4.27 trillion won for a new plant at its Sejong site, and 2.51 trillion won for its Vietnam subsidiary, marking the company's largest-ever investment in a single product.

articles.title: CERN Releases "colibri," a Vendor-Independent VHDL Common Library for FPGAs
articles.summary: CERN's EP department released colibri, a VHDL common library built up over four years after gateware designers found themselves relying on homebrew tools scattered across FPGAs from multiple vendors.

articles.title: Enterprise Red Hat Linux Support for ROS 2
articles.summary: Red Hat Enterprise Linux has officially achieved Tier 1 support status in the Robot Operating System 2 development ecosystem, beginning with the Rolling Ridley release.
